supports_model.mismatch_notes: h_g and sigma equal Bartz Eqs. [7] and [5] (SI with g_c = 1; properties at chamber stagnation conditions). Pr estimate equals Eq. [8]. Viscosity estimator uses 1.1929e-7 where the exact SI conversion of Eq. [9] (46.6e-10 lb/(in s) x 17.85797 x 1.8^0.6) is 1.18407e-7, i.e. 0.746% high (0.149% in h_g); code docstrings cite SP-125 'Eq. 4-23' and 'Eq. 4-18' but the SP-125 equations are 4-16 and 4-15 (PDF p.110). Recovery temperature uses r = Pr^(1/3) (not in Bartz; SP-125 p.109 defines T_aw as (T_c)ns x recovery factor 0.90-0.98). Bartz's applicability statements (D*/r_c <= ~3; angles within 50% of 30/15 deg; chamber fluxes 40-50% of measured) are not enforced.

model_review.citation_vs_support: Registry cites Bartz 1957 (local technical-notes-1957.pdf), which contains Eqs. [5], [7], [8], [9] (PDF pp.1-2). Code docstring equation numbers for SP-125 are wrong (see comparison).
model_review.physical_validation: NOT_ESTABLISHED: Bartz calibrates C against one boundary-layer calculation and says the meager experimental data neither support nor deny it.
model_review.sensitivity: mu coefficient error changes h_g by 0.149%; validity-domain issues may matter more (chamber under-prediction).
model_review.physics_finding: Formula transcription is correct. Recommended (not applied; code edits forbidden this session): correct the viscosity coefficient to 1.18407e-7 or drop the 'exact' claim, fix the two SP-125 equation numbers, and report Bartz's D*/r_c and chamber-flux applicability limits.
remaining_uncertainties: chamber-section heat flux (Bartz: 40-50% of measured for RFNA-NH3)
D*/r_c and wall-angle range of the design versus Bartz's stated range
property evaluation (stagnation vs mean film) for propellants unlike RFNA-N2H4
recovery-factor definition differs between SP-125 and the code

equations.label: Bartz 1957 Eq. [1] mass-velocity scaling
equations.quote: might serve as the desired rough approximation equation
equations.description: Rough approximation: h_g dominated by mass flow rate per unit area.

equations.label: Bartz 1957 Eq. [2] pipe-flow Nusselt form
equations.quote: which happens to be the same form as the equation that has
equations.description: Nondimensional form of Eq. [1]; m = 0.8, n arbitrarily 0.4.

equations.label: Bartz 1957 Eq. [3] h_g with arithmetic-mean properties
equations.quote: With these assumptions, Equation [2] can be solved for hg to give
equations.description: Properties at the arithmetic mean of bulk and wall temperature.

equations.label: Bartz 1957 Eq. [4] h_g with stagnation properties and sigma
equations.description: C_p and Pr constant at stagnation values; sigma carries all property-variation corrections.
assumptions: C_p and Pr do not vary appreciably with temperature

equations.label: Bartz 1957 Eq. [5] property-variation factor sigma
equations.quote: contains all the corrections for property variation across the boundary layer
equations.description: Sigma from T_am = (T + T_w)/2, rho ~ 1/T and mu ~ T^omega, in terms of T_0, T_w and M.

equations.label: Bartz 1957 Eq. [6] h_g in terms of C* and area ratio
equations.quote: The equation for hg can be put in a form more easily used for rocket nozzle computations
equations.description: rho'U expressed through C* and A*/A; bracket constant through a nozzle.

equations.label: Bartz 1957 Eq. [7] final rapid-estimation equation
equations.quote: a factor to account for the effect of radius of curvature of the nozzle throat
equations.description: Eq. [6] with C = 0.026 and the throat-curvature factor (D*/r_c)^0.1.
validity: comparison nozzle: D*/r_c about 1, contraction/expansion half angles 30 and 15 deg; probably sufficiently accurate if angles change by no more than 50% and D*/r_c is not greater than about 3

equations.label: Bartz 1957 Eq. [8] kinetic-theory Prandtl number
equations.quote: kinetic theory (5) can be used to get the approximate result
equations.description: Approximate Pr when data are unavailable (kinetic theory).

equations.label: Bartz 1957 Eq. [9] viscosity correlation
equations.quote: data for the viscosity of air at high temperatures can be used
equations.description: Correlation from NBS air data; reasonably accurate for mixtures consisting principally of diatomic gases.

claims.subject: Bartz constant C
claims.object: matching Eq. [6] at the throat of one nozzle to a turbulent boundary-layer calculation: C = 0.026
claims.statement: C was determined by equating h_g from Eq. [6] at the throat of a particular nozzle with the turbulent boundary-layer analysis of Reference 2 (case 2a) for the same mass flow and gas properties; the resulting C = 0.026 is coincidentally close to the usual turbulent pipe-flow value.
qualifiers: single-nozzle calibration against a calculation, not experiment
claims.quote: The resulting value of C was found to be 0.026

claims.subject: Eq. [7] applicability
claims.object: if contraction and expansion angles change by no more than 50% from 30/15 deg and D*/r_c is not greater than about 3
claims.statement: The comparison nozzle had D*/r_c about unity and contraction and expansion half angles of 30 and 15 deg; nozzles with different angles will probably not show the same agreement, but the equation will probably be sufficiently accurate if the angles change by no more than 50 per cent and D*/r_c is not greater than about 3.
claims.quote: contraction and expansion angles are not changed by more than 50 per cent

claims.subject: Eq. [7] in the chamber
claims.object: chamber heat fluxes for RFNA-NH3 tests: only 40-50% of measured (nozzle average fluxes agreed)
claims.statement: Average nozzle heat flux from Eq. [7] agreed well with RFNA-NH3 measurements over a wide range of chamber pressures, but the equation was notably unsuccessful for chamber heat fluxes, predicting only 40-50 per cent of the measured values; near the throat and beyond, predictions are expected to be too low with strong radiators, dissociation-recombination or high-frequency instabilities, and too high with insulating deposits or incomplete combustion.
claims.quote: the values being only 40-50 per cent of the measured values

claims.subject: experimental comparison
claims.object: supporting or denying the equation; agreement is with one boundary-layer calculation and meager rocket data
claims.statement: Bartz states that the RFNA-N2H4 experimental data should not be construed as supporting or denying either method; additional reliable local data are needed.
claims.quote: These experimental data should not be construed as supporting or denying
